meta.title: Annex 14 Vol I legacy OLS vs Amendment 18 OFS/OES dimensions
meta.source: ICAO Annex 14 Vol I Chapter 1 (1.6, 1.8) and Chapter 4, legacy text and Amendment 18 (27/11/25), as supplied by Dan Parsons

conventions.units: metres; slopes and divergences as fractions (0.0333 = 3.33%)
conventions.strings: textual values are dynamic references resolved by the geometry engine (e.g. 'End of strip (a)', '½ approach inner edge')
conventions.legacy_ihs: arcs centred on runway strip ends joined by tangents; height above aerodrome elevation (decision L2)
conventions.new_horizontal_oes: arcs centred on thresholds joined by tangents; height above aerodrome elevation
conventions.transitional_offsets: new transitional lower edge at ½ approach inner edge from CL (after modifiers); inner transitional at ½ inner approach inner edge

adg.basis: Vat (kt) and wingspan (m); all bounds are 'up to but not including'

decisions_and_open_questions.question: Resolved by the clause text: lower edge comes down the approach side to the inner edge end, then runs parallel to CL. Offset = ½ approach inner edge, after width footnotes.
Same construction via the inner approach side (4.2.4.2 a 1; 4.2.4.3 a for PA).
Inner approach is a rectangular portion of the approach surface; no slope tabled.
decisions_and_open_questions.decision: Same slope as the OFS approach surface

decisions_and_open_questions.topic: Inner approach vs approach inner edge
decisions_and_open_questions.question: Inner approach can be narrower than the approach inner edge (e.g. instrument ADG III 175 m vs 120 m), so the inner transitional sits inside the transitional by half the difference. Draw both, overlaid.
Table 4-6 IV/V 5 m below III 10 m.
Longer sides run 5 350 m beyond each threshold, so the rectangle spans runway length + 10 700 m; shorter side 7 410 m centred on CL.
Table 4-11 lower section length.
